newsitem.title: MEXICO: Kimberly Clark de Mexico 9 mo. net rises.
newsitem.headline: Kimberly Clark de Mexico 9 mo. net rises.

text.p: Mexican paper firm Kimberly Clark de Mexico SA said it earned a nine-month net profit of 1.4896 billion pesos, up from 1.1732 billion during the same period of 1995.
The company, an affiliate of the U.S. paper giant Kimberly-Clark Corp, said its earnings per share for the period were 5.54 pesos and $11.08 per ADS.
The company said in a statement its operating profit for the first nine months was 1.8349 billion pesos versus 1.7053 billion during the first nine months of last year.

Kimberly-Clark said its income statement includes second and third quarter results from Compania Industrial de San Cristobal (Crisoba), the subsidiary of Scott Paper Co that was purchased by Kimberly-Clark de Mexico at the end of the first quarter.
The company offered additional information prepared to show the combined results of both companies as if they were one during the nine-month period.
It said net profits during the first nine months would have been 1.581 billion pesos, down from 1.648 billion pesos during the year-ago period.
Operating profits would have been 1.9726 billion pesos versus 2.2387 billion, and sales would have been 7.221 billion pesos versus 8.553 billion pesos during the same period of 1995.
Kimberly Clark said combined sales for the two companies decreased due to reduced prices of pulp and paper consumer products and the Mexican economic recession, which affected the product mix.
It said the third quarter showed a 12 percent sales volume increase.
Operating income margin as a percentage of sales increased one percentage point as a result of strict cost controls and synergies now being realized from the merger, it said.

It said the 1.581 billion net profit figure was helped by non-cash financial items, especially due to the stability of the peso and interest earned on investments. It said a greater tax provision had also been booked in to bring Crisoba's accounting practices in line with Kimberly Clark's.

"The pooling and integration of Crisoba and Kimber is moving forward according to plan with synergies being realized in the second half of the year. The approved brand and asset divestitute plan is being executed and the sale of the "Baby Fresh" brand was completed during the third quarter ... and in early October, the feminine care business (Sancela) was also sold," it said.
